--- title: "Quarterback yardage keeps climbing across a college career while running back and receiver production plateaus after the third season" date: "2026-11-05" description: "Across quarterbacks, running backs and receivers, median passing yardage rises through every career season in the data while rushing and receiving yardage levels off after the third, and all three fall against higher-rated opponents." followups: - "Position-specific baselines: adjust each group against its own position rather than every player with a line in the category." - "Split the career arcs by whether a player was eventually drafted, to see when the drafted and undrafted paths separate." - "Carry a second stat per group (quarterback rushing, running back receiving) so a group is not reduced to one dimension." author: - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco" freeze: auto vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Quarterback yardage keeps climbing across a college career while running back and receiver production plateaus after the third season} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Load the package from the checkout with pkgload; no package install is # required. Under altdoc the render runs in a temp dir, so resolve the root # first (CFB2NFL_ROOT in the site build, else walk up to the _targets store). root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT", "") if (!nzchar(root)) { dir <- getwd() while (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets")) && dirname(dir) != dir) { dir <- dirname(dir) } root <- if (file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets"))) dir else getwd() } knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root) pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE) con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"), read_only = TRUE ) library(DBI) library(dplyr) library(duckdb) library(ggiraph) library(ggplot2) library(knitr) # One interaction style for every girafe figure: a clear hover pop, dimming # of non-hovered marks, a dark tooltip, and toolbar zoom + PNG download. set_girafe_defaults( opts_hover = opts_hover( css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);" ), opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"), opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip( css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;" ), opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5), opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"), opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE) ) # thousands-separated and percent formatters for inline numbers fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) { formatC(as.numeric(x), big.mark = ",", format = "f", digits = digits) } pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Season arcs and game production are built here from the tested package # functions (decision 0037). The season index counts every season with any # stat line, so the arcs need the full long stats, not just the yardage rows. # Roster carries the position label used to form the three groups. pg <- dbReadTable(con, "player_game") sa <- dbGetQuery( con, "SELECT playerId, player, season, team, category, statType, stat FROM player_stats" ) |> build_season_arcs() gp <- build_game_production(pg) rost <- dbReadTable(con, "roster") band_levels <- c( "Under 1400", "1400 to 1599", "1600 to 1799", "1800 and up", "Unrated" ) group_levels <- c("Quarterbacks", "Running backs", "Receivers") # Each position group is tracked by one signature yardage stat: a quarterback # by passing, a running back by rushing, a receiver by receiving. The group # palette is reused in every figure so group always means the same colour. sig <- tibble::tribble( ~pos , ~group , ~game_stat , ~category , ~label , "QB" , "Quarterbacks" , "pass_yds" , "passing" , "Passing yards" , "RB" , "Running backs" , "rush_yds" , "rushing" , "Rushing yards" , "WR" , "Receivers" , "rec_yds" , "receiving" , "Receiving yards" ) group_pal <- c( Quarterbacks = "#4C78A8", `Running backs` = "#E45756", Receivers = "#54A24B" ) # One group per player: the position he appears at most often on a roster, # restricted to the three offensive skill positions (key on athlete id). pos <- rost |> filter(.data$position %in% c("QB", "RB", "WR")) |> count(.data$playerId, .data$position) |> group_by(.data$playerId) |> slice_max(.data$n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup() |> transmute(.data$playerId, pos = .data$position) # Signature season arcs: season totals in each group's signature category. cast_sa <- sa |> filter(.data$statType == "YDS") |> inner_join(pos, by = "playerId") |> inner_join( sig |> select("pos", "category", "group", "label"), by = c("pos", "category") ) |> mutate(group = factor(.data$group, group_levels)) # Signature game production, carrying the opponent-adjusted residual. cast_gp <- gp |> inner_join(pos, by = "playerId") |> inner_join( sig |> select("pos", game_stat = "game_stat", "group"), by = c("pos", stat = "game_stat") ) |> mutate( group = factor(.data$group, group_levels), band = factor(.data$opponent_elo_band, band_levels) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Every figure and inline number is computed here from the database. # Opponent Elo distribution and the band each cutoff carves out. The cutoffs # are even 200-point Elo steps (1400 / 1600 / 1800); this shows how many games # and what Elo range land in each so the choice can be read off the data. elo_median <- median(pg$opponent_pregame_elo, na.rm = TRUE) elo_bands <- pg |> mutate( band = factor(opponent_elo_band(.data$opponent_pregame_elo), band_levels) ) |> group_by(.data$band) |> summarise( games = dplyr::n(), min_elo = min(.data$opponent_pregame_elo), max_elo = max(.data$opponent_pregame_elo), .groups = "drop" ) |> arrange(.data$band) # Population of each group: distinct players, season lines, and game lines. grp_pop <- sig |> mutate(group = factor(.data$group, group_levels)) |> select("group", "label") |> left_join( cast_sa |> group_by(.data$group) |> summarise( players = dplyr::n_distinct(.data$playerId), season_lines = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ), by = "group" ) |> left_join( cast_gp |> count(.data$group, name = "game_lines"), by = "group" ) |> arrange(.data$group) # Viz 1: career arcs. Median signature yards by career season, keeping only the # season indices where every group still has at least 50 players. arc_n <- cast_sa |> count(.data$group, .data$season_index) keep_idx <- arc_n |> group_by(.data$season_index) |> summarise(m = min(.data$n), .groups = "drop") |> filter(.data$m >= 50) |> pull(.data$season_index) arc_med <- cast_sa |> filter(.data$season_index %in% keep_idx) |> group_by(.data$group, .data$season_index) |> summarise( med = median(.data$value), q1 = quantile(.data$value, 0.25), q3 = quantile(.data$value, 0.75), players = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ) max_idx <- max(keep_idx) qb_arc <- arc_med |> filter(.data$group == "Quarterbacks") qb_med_1 <- qb_arc$med[qb_arc$season_index == 1] qb_med_max <- qb_arc$med[qb_arc$season_index == max_idx] rb_arc <- arc_med |> filter(.data$group == "Running backs") rb_med_peak <- max(rb_arc$med) # Viz 2: opponent-band gradient. Mean signature yards per game by group x band, # with a +/- 1 SD range marking how much games vary within each band. band_grad <- cast_gp |> group_by(.data$group, .data$band) |> summarise( mean_yds = mean(.data$value), sd_yds = sd(.data$value), games = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate( lo = pmax(.data$mean_yds - .data$sd_yds, 0), hi = .data$mean_yds + .data$sd_yds ) rated <- band_grad |> filter(.data$band != "Unrated") drop_tbl <- rated |> group_by(.data$group) |> summarise( drop = mean_yds[.data$band == "Under 1400"] - mean_yds[.data$band == "1800 and up"], .groups = "drop" ) qb_drop <- drop_tbl$drop[drop_tbl$group == "Quarterbacks"] rb_drop <- drop_tbl$drop[drop_tbl$group == "Running backs"] wr_drop <- drop_tbl$drop[drop_tbl$group == "Receivers"] # Viz 3: residual spread. The residual is opponent- and season-adjusted, so it # centres near zero by construction; the spread is what differs by group. resid_spread <- cast_gp |> group_by(.data$group) |> summarise( games = dplyr::n(), sd = sd(.data$residual), iqr = IQR(.data$residual), p90 = quantile(.data$residual, 0.9), .groups = "drop" ) qb_sd <- resid_spread$sd[resid_spread$group == "Quarterbacks"] wr_sd <- resid_spread$sd[resid_spread$group == "Receivers"] # Per-group x band residual summary, for the exploratory boxplot tooltips. resid_box <- cast_gp |> group_by(.data$group, .data$band) |> summarise( med = median(.data$residual), q1 = quantile(.data$residual, 0.25), q3 = quantile(.data$residual, 0.75), games = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate( tip = paste0( .data$group, ", ", .data$band, ": median ", fmt(.data$med), ", IQR ", fmt(.data$q1), " to ", fmt(.data$q3), " over ", fmt(.data$games), " games" ) ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-11-05. Careers of recent classes are right-censored; later seasons may not yet be present.* ::: ## 1. Introduction A player's yardage moves from season to season and game to game, and both the stage of his career and the strength of his opponent are reasons. This post follows three offensive groups, quarterbacks, running backs and receivers, and asks three descriptive questions of the data: how does each group's production grow across a college career, how does it change as opponents get stronger, and how much does it swing from game to game once opponent strength is held constant. ## 2. Data ### 2.1 Each game is set against the league baseline for its opponent strength Each player-game is compared with the average for the same season, stat and opponent band. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Term , ~Meaning , "Position group" , "Quarterbacks, running backs, or receivers, from the player's most frequent roster position." , "Signature stat" , "The yardage that defines a group: passing (QB), rushing (RB), receiving (WR)." , "Season arc" , "Season total of the signature stat, one per season." , "Season index" , "The player's n-th season with a stat line in the data (career season)." , "Opponent band" , "The opponent's pregame Elo: under 1400, 1400 to 1599, 1600 to 1799, 1800 and up, or unrated (no Elo)." , "Baseline" , "Mean yards for that season, band, and stat across all players with a line in the category." , "Residual" , "A game's yards minus its baseline." ) |> kable(caption = "The terms used in the post.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The terms used in the post. |Term |Meaning | |:--------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |Position group |Quarterbacks, running backs, or receivers, from the player's most frequent roster position. | |Signature stat |The yardage that defines a group: passing (QB), rushing (RB), receiving (WR). | |Season arc |Season total of the signature stat, one per season. | |Season index |The player's n-th season with a stat line in the data (career season). | |Opponent band |The opponent's pregame Elo: under 1400, 1400 to 1599, 1600 to 1799, 1800 and up, or unrated (no Elo). | |Baseline |Mean yards for that season, band, and stat across all players with a line in the category. | |Residual |A game's yards minus its baseline. | ::: ::: ### 2.2 Opponent Elo is split into even 200-point bands Elo is CFBD's pregame team-strength rating: a higher number is a stronger opponent, and the rating is recentred each week so the median rated team sits near 1,512. The bands are even 200-point steps at 1400, 1600 and 1800, chosen so each covers the same width of the scale rather than the same number of games. The table and histogram below show the resulting split: opponents CFBD does not rate (mostly FCS and lower-division teams) have no Elo and form their own unrated band rather than being dropped. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} elo_bands |> transmute( `Opponent band` = .data$band, `Player-games` = fmt(.data$games), `Lowest Elo` = ifelse(is.finite(.data$min_elo), fmt(.data$min_elo), "--"), `Highest Elo` = ifelse(is.finite(.data$max_elo), fmt(.data$max_elo), "--") ) |> kable(caption = "Games and Elo range in each opponent band.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Games and Elo range in each opponent band. |Opponent band |Player-games |Lowest Elo |Highest Elo | |:-------------|:------------|:----------|:-----------| |Under 1400 |63,970 |528 |1,399 | |1400 to 1599 |61,415 |1,400 |1,599 | |1600 to 1799 |46,995 |1,600 |1,799 | |1800 and up |23,229 |1,800 |2,415 | |Unrated |71,208 |-- |-- | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pg |> filter(!is.na(.data$opponent_pregame_elo)) |> ggplot(aes(.data$opponent_pregame_elo)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 25, fill = "#4C78A8") + geom_vline( xintercept = c(1400, 1600, 1800), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8 ) + annotate( "text", x = c(1300, 1500, 1700, 2000), y = Inf, vjust = 1.6, label = c("Under 1400", "1400 to 1599", "1600 to 1799", "1800 and up"), size = 4 ) + labs(x = "Opponent pregame Elo", y = "Player-games") + theme_cfb2nfl() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](2026-11-05-performance-arcs_files/figure-html/s22-hist-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### 2.3 Each group is tracked by one signature stat A quarterback is read by his passing yards, a running back by his rushing yards, and a receiver by his receiving yards. All three groups are large enough to summarise. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} grp_pop |> transmute( `Position group` = .data$group, `Signature stat` = .data$label, Players = fmt(.data$players), `Season lines` = fmt(.data$season_lines), `Game lines` = fmt(.data$game_lines) ) |> kable(caption = "The three groups and the size of each population.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The three groups and the size of each population. |Position group |Signature stat |Players |Season lines |Game lines | |:--------------|:---------------|:-------|:------------|:----------| |Quarterbacks |Passing yards |3,602 |8,869 |33,454 | |Running backs |Rushing yards |6,542 |16,085 |25,303 | |Receivers |Receiving yards |10,845 |25,562 |27,778 | ::: ::: ## 3. Results ### 3.1 Quarterback yardage keeps climbing across a career while running backs and receivers plateau Median passing yards rise at every career season shown, from 119 in a quarterback's first season to 1,706 by his 6th, while rushing and receiving medians flatten after about the third season near 282 yards. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} arc_med |> transmute( `Position group` = .data$group, `Season index` = .data$season_index, `Median yards` = fmt(.data$med), `Middle 50%` = paste0(fmt(.data$q1), " to ", fmt(.data$q3)), Players = fmt(.data$players) ) |> arrange(`Position group`, `Season index`) |> kable( caption = "Median signature yards by career season, with the middle 50% range." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Median signature yards by career season, with |Running backs | 5|270 |102 to 594 |511 | |Running backs | 6|253 |112 to 447 |115 | |Receivers | 1|50 |15 to 166 |9,947 | |Receivers | 2|130 |36 to 349 |7,282 | |Receivers | 3|208 |60 to 480 |4,802 | |Receivers | 4|282 |92 to 535 |2,694 | |Receivers | 5|286 |104 to 544 |711 | |Receivers | 6|304 |136 to 553 |120 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- arc_med |> mutate( tooltip = paste0( same season and opponent band. $$\text{residual} = \text{game yards} - \text{baseline (season, band)}$$ Because the baseline already removes season and opponent strength, residuals centre near zero for every group; what differs is their spread, widest for quarterbacks (standard deviation 96 yards) and narrowest for receivers (42 yards). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} resid_spread |> transmute( ``` ::: ::: ## 4. Summary The three groups behave differently along all three axes the post looked at. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Question , ~`What the data showed` , "How does production grow across a career?" , paste0("Quarterback median passing yards rose every career season (", fmt(qb_med_1), " to ", fmt(qb_med_max), "); rushing and receiving plateaued after the third.") , "How does it change against stronger opponents?" , paste0("Mean yards per game fell from the weakest to strongest rated band for all three, steepest for running backs (", fmt(rb_drop), " yards).") , "How much does it swing game to game?" , paste0("Opponent-adjusted residuals centre near zero but spread widest for quarterbacks (SD ", fmt(qb_sd, 1), ") and narrowest for receivers (SD ", fmt(wr_sd, 1), ").") ) |> kable(caption = "Each question and what the data showed.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Each question and what the data showed. |Question |What the data showed | |:----------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |How does production grow across a career? |Quarterback median passing yards rose every career season (119 to 1,706); rushing and receiving plateaued after the third. | |How does it change against stronger opponents? |Mean yards per game fell from the weakest to strongest rated band for all three, steepest for running backs (19 yards). | |How much does it swing game to game? |Opponent-adjusted residuals centre near zero but spread widest for quarterbacks (SD 96.3) and narrowest for receivers (SD 42.2). | ::: ::: ## 5. Discussion ::: {.callout-important} Production grows across a career for quarterbacks in a way it does not for running backs or receivers, whose medians level off after the third season. All three groups produce less against stronger opponents, and once that is removed quarterback output remains the most volatile from game to game. ::: Caveats: the baseline pools every player with a line in the category rather than comparing within position, so a running back's receiving-band baseline mixes in receivers; a position-specific baseline is a natural refinement. Groups are assigned from a player's most frequent roster position and a group is reduced to one signature stat, so a quarterback's rushing or a running back's receiving is set aside. Game-level stats begin around 2013, so the game exhibits cover fewer seasons than the career arcs. Unrated opponents (no Elo, mostly lower-division teams) are kept as their own band rather than dropped. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE) ``` :::
